necessarily being root. Timestamp invalidation is authentication cleanup, not
restoration of another process or file. See the [sudo manual](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/sudo/sudo.8.en.html).

## LPRIV-02. Attributes become process credentials only under the right conditions

GNU Bash can drop a differing effective identity unless privileged mode is used.
Long options are placed before `-p`. File capability effectiveness, mount flags,
NoNewPrivs and namespaces affect exec credential transitions. SETUID is different
from unrestricted filesystem access. The Python call changes the process UID;
the subsequent shell must corroborate it and the host boundary.

Sources: [Bash manual](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/bash/bash.1.en.html),
[Linux capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html),
[execve](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/execve.2.html), and
[Python os.setuid](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.setuid).
Zsh's `-p` retains privileged startup mode, while `-f` disables RCS after
the mandatory system startup file. Different real and effective IDs are a
normal possible SUID result. See [Zsh options](https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Options.html)
and [Zsh startup files](https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/Files.html).
The GDB branch uses the build's embedded Python, with `-nx` and no inferior.
`os.execl` replaces the debugger directly. The initial UID tuple and final shell
identity are separate results; a root-looking GDB prompt is neither. See
[GDB Python commands](https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Python-Commands.html),
[GDB mode options](https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Mode-Options.html)
and [Python exec functions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.execl).
The PHP branch uses the CLI `-r` form and requires the `pcntl_exec` function on
the **same** SUID binary. `pcntl_exec` replaces its process on success; a
function check, inherited file owner or absent return value is not a shell
identity result. The target's `/bin/sh -p` support and real/effective UID must
be checked separately. See [PHP CLI options](https://www.php.net/manual/en/features.commandline.options.php)
and [pcntl_exec](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.pcntl-exec.php).
Permitted-only capabilities, other binaries and container escape require distinct
procedures; these examples do not close those coverage gaps.

## LPRIV-03. Demonstrate the consumer, then undo the exact change

The working sequence is inspect/backup, guarded append, natural-trigger proof,
then restore/cleanup. Each command repeats literal placeholders rather than
depending on prior shell variables. The backup and expected copy are this
operation's state, not reusable setup for unrelated checklist steps.

The byte backup does not restore metadata. In-place writing avoids replacing a
root-owned inode with the user's copy, but writes can clear security attributes.
Do not use this procedure where those attributes exist or metadata restoration
is uncertain. A disposable-lab reset is recovery, not evidence of exact restoration.
Never recursively remove the temporary root or delete recovery copies early.

The append now checks ACL as well as bytes and metadata and compares the result
to the prepared expected copy. These checks detect selected changes; they do not
lock the file or make concurrent scheduler execution race-free. Partial appends,
path changes or a running consumer require recovery rather than an automatic retry.

The expected copy lets the restore guard distinguish this proof from a concurrent
edit. ACL capture must succeed before comparison; two empty files left by failed
commands are not permission evidence. Restoration writes into the original inode
and confirms the bytes rather than replacing it with a user-owned backup. Mode
0644 permits reading the proof while its directory remains private mode 0700.

The proof exercises the actual scheduled execution context rather than inferring
it from ownership or a configured user. A private directory avoids an unrelated
user pre-creating the proof path. Its owner can inspect/remove the named proof even
when the scheduler created the file under a different UID. Filesystem restrictions
or sandboxing can prevent that behavior and must remain explicit.

Appending may never execute if the script exits early. In-place restoration can
also interact with extended attributes or concurrently running consumers; record
those before testing and restore/verify the real state, not only bytes. This
procedure deliberately avoids manufacturing a SUID binary or persistent root
job. Confirmed privileged execution still requires a separate reviewed foothold
method if an interactive session is the next objective.

## LPRIV-04. A capability is an operation-specific boundary

Optional diagnostics when an actual operation fails or its boundary is unclear:

```bash
findmnt -T '<absolute-observed-capability-bearing-executable>' -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
grep -E '^(Uid|Gid|CapEff|CapBnd|NoNewPrivs|Seccomp):' /proc/self/status
capsh --print 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,24p' || printf 'capsh unavailable; retain partial capability evidence.\n'
```

Optional low-port reference, only for a specific authorized question and recorded
`cap_net_bind_service=ep` on this Python 3 executable. Use an unused loopback port:

```bash
'<same-observed-capability-bearing-python3>' - '<unused-loopback-port-below-1024>' <<'PY'
import socket, sys
port = int(sys.argv[1])
if not 1 <= port <= 1023:
    raise SystemExit('Choose an unused port below 1024')
sock = socket.socket()
try:
    sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
    print("loopback bind succeeded")
finally:
    sock.close()
PY
printf 'Capability probe exit: %s\n' "$?"
```

The socket closes immediately, including on error. A success is not a shell or
proof that the file capability caused the bind. Existing process rights and
kernel policy can permit it independently; keep attribution unresolved when
they are unknown. Occupied ports and denied operations also remain ambiguous.
Do not listen, accept connections or use a network-facing address. Return to
LPRIV-04's result choices after the selected check.

Linux file capabilities attach to an executable and can be filtered by the mount,
process bounding set, `NoNewPrivs` and namespace. `cap_net_bind_service` can allow
a low loopback port without granting root. A successful bind also needs attribution
to the tested process and an unused port. Do not turn a harmless bind into a generic
recipe for file reads, UID changes or container escape. Other capabilities need
their own observed operation and rollback analysis.

## LPRIV-05. A service unit is not proof of a running privileged consumer

`systemctl cat` may be superseded by drop-ins, and `ExecStart` can contain an
interpreter, arguments or an environment expansion. `User=` and `Group=` identify
the configured service account, while an unset value follows manager defaults.
The unit can be inactive, masked or replaced before a trigger. This procedure
deliberately stops before restart or path modification. A writable service path is
a lead requiring a separate, reversible procedure, not a privilege assertion.

## LPRIV-06. Child execution depends on the complete sudo rule

The executable name alone is insufficient. Match run-as user/group, allowed
arguments, exclusions and inherited policy. A required non-default run-as group
needs its exact permitted `-g` value; these examples do not assume one. Fixed
script/path rules are not unrestricted Python or find delegation.
NOEXEC can block child execution, while INTERCEPT can check the child against
sudoers. Keep a denial rather than treating it as a reason to disable controls.
See the [upstream sudoers manual](https://www.sudo.ws/docs/man/1.9.14/sudoers.man.pdf).

GNU find's `-exec` receives arguments through the terminating literal semicolon.
The escaped `\;` prevents the parent shell from consuming it. With one start
path and `-maxdepth 0`, the action concerns that path only, not a recursive scan.
See [GNU find depth limits](https://www.gnu.org/software/findutils/manual/html_node/find_html/Directories.html)
and [command actions](https://www.gnu.org/software/findutils/manual/html_node/find_html/Single-File.html).

Python's `os.execl` replaces the interpreter with the supplied Bash executable;
it does not call `setuid` or create an additional network channel. Python `-I`
limits ordinary Python search-path/environment customization, not sudo policy.
See [Python exec functions](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.execl)
and [isolated mode](https://docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html#cmdoption-I).
The new shell's observed identity, not the delegated executable's output or exit
status, determines the result. Native sudo policy and terminal behavior still
need live authorized trials; mock argv tests are not privilege verification.

GNU time runs one supplied command with its remaining arguments and reports
resource use after that command exits. The working example does not use output
or append options, so it creates no timing file. Its report is not privilege
proof. See [GNU time invocation](https://www.gnu.org/software/time/manual/html_node/Invoking-time.html).

Perl's explicit `exec PROGRAM LIST` form replaces the interpreter with the
named program and arguments. The code uses the first literal argument as that
program, so a path containing spaces remains one argument. It does not invoke
an intermediate shell to parse a command string. A blocked exec is an error,
not a reason to disable sudo policy. See [Perl exec](https://perldoc.perl.org/functions/exec).
GNU nice runs its supplied child with adjusted niceness. A valid command can
inherit the delegated effective identity, but scheduling output proves neither
identity nor host attribution. Restricted child paths still need a matching
procedure. See [GNU nice invocation](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/nice-invocation.html).

## LPRIV-07. Temporary SUID access is a separate, higher-impact choice

The verified root consumer creates a new executable through GNU install. Numeric
mode 4755 requests owner SUID and executable/readable bits; the fresh private
directory limits ordinary traversal to its owner and root. A root-owned SUID
artifact still exists until explicitly removed. This is why the entry requires
disposable-lab permission rather than silently upgrading an id proof.
See [GNU install options](https://manpages.debian.org/testing/coreutils/install.1.en.html).

Bash `-p` retains an effective identity provided by execution; it does not create
root from an ordinary copy. nosuid, noexec, NoNewPrivs and namespaces can block or
limit the transition. See [Bash privileged mode](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html).
The source binary must already be attributable GNU Bash, not an arbitrary file
that merely has a Bash-like filename.

The appended command refuses a pre-existing destination, including dangling
symlinks. This is not a filesystem lock or a race-free scheduler protocol.
Independent bytes/owner/mode and shell identity checks remain necessary. Restore
the scheduled source first to prevent later recreation, then remove the exact
privileged artifact. Unexpected concurrent edits preserve recovery copies.
No root scheduler, install/SUID creation or resulting shell has been live tested.

## LPRIV-08. Client authority and server authority are different

The FunboxEasyEnum source first puts a shell command at the SQL prompt and
receives a syntax error, then uses the client's `\!` command and obtains
native uid0. The child executes under the local client process's authority.
Neither SQL grants nor a remote database username explains that host privilege.
The checklist uses an observed local socket and separate native identity proof
to avoid merging those contexts.

Client version and policy matter. MariaDB sandbox mode disables `system`, and
MySQL versions can disable client commands or the system command. A disabled
feature is a failed prerequisite here, not permission to enable it. The shown
connection uses the known local socket/account, no SQL mutation, no auto-rehash
inventory and no reconnect loop. Client login/history behavior still needs a
native authorized trial. See [MariaDB client commands and sandbox](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/clients-and-utilities/mariadb-client/mariadb-command-line-client)
and [MySQL client commands](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/9.7/en/mysql-commands.html).

## LPRIV-09. Encoding transports bytes, not authority

An existing SUID encoder may open a file under its owner's effective identity.
Decoding its output does not change the calling shell's identity. The extra
8193rd byte detects an over-budget result even when a small producer finishes
before the output limiter closes. `pipefail` also preserves encoder/decoder
failures; normal SIGPIPE from a stopped large stream is not complete success.
Mode 600 and a private parent protect the new copy, while noclobber prevents
overwriting an existing path. These shell checks do not eliminate races in an
untrusted parent, so a shared directory is not an acceptable destination.
See [GNU base32](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/base32-invocation.html).
Native SUID read validation remains pending; ordinary round-trip fixtures test
the capture boundary, not privileged filesystem access.

## LPRIV-10. A no-index diff reads without staging

Git's `diff --no-index` compares filesystem paths and implies exit-code mode.
Against `/dev/null`, ordinary nonempty text appears as added lines and exits 1.
Empty-file creation metadata can also differ, and file-open errors may use 1.
Only the actual diff plus absence of errors supports the read result.
`--no-pager`, `--no-ext-diff` and `--no-textconv` prevent this procedure from
becoming a pager or configured external-filter shell. `--text` makes the read
inspectable, while `cat -v` renders control bytes visibly. This is a file-read
procedure, not the source prose's unshown pager escape. No root-level Git init,
staging, privileged shell or credential success is asserted. A large input can
still cost Git memory despite the display bound. See
[Git diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff).

## LPRIV-11. A missing delegated script differs from a scheduled consumer

The sudo rule is the immediate consumer. Creating the exact absent file supplies
its bytes, but only invocation plus native target/run-as identity establishes
the transition. Fresh-file noclobber prevents an overwrite; inode/metadata/hash
checks detect changed state before execution and cleanup. They do not make a
shared parent race-free, so the trusted-parent prerequisite remains mandatory.
No new SUID permission is introduced. This is source-triggered manual authoring,
not a live reproduction of SoSimple or an autonomous app action.

For nice argument paths, sudoers wildcard matching and filesystem path resolution
are different operations. An argument wildcard can match slashes and spaces;
matching it does not verify the resolved executable. Keep both the literal
argument and canonical target. See [sudoers wildcard rules](https://www.sudo.ws/docs/man/1.9.14/sudoers.man.pdf).

## LPRIV-12. The installed dispatcher determines the operation

The Debian wrapper has different paths for standard service actions and its
SysV fallback. The latter can execute an init-directory-relative path, while
standard actions can dispatch to systemctl or update OpenRC bookkeeping.
Inspect the actual target implementation before using a relative shell name.
Environment clearing and a changed working directory also do not establish the
run-as account; native identity does. This branch neither manages a real service
nor claims every service wrapper supports the same behavior. See
[Debian service source](https://sources.debian.org/src/init-system-helpers/1.69/script/service)
and [service manual](https://manpages.debian.org/bookworm/init-system-helpers/service.8.en.html).

## LPRIV-13. Account text and numeric process authority differ

Inclusiveness's reviewed program asks a PATH-resolved command for account text,
then separately changes identity and opens a shell. The helper satisfies that
text check only. Its output is never independent identity evidence; an absolute
native `id` and the actual shell's numeric process status establish the result.
Do not apply this to every SUID binary or assume neighboring source matches it.

The `p` exec variants search PATH for names without a slash; a command-scoped
PATH reaches descendants without altering the original parent environment.
See [Linux exec path lookup](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/exec.3.html).
The reviewed `setuid` call still must succeed. Real/effective/saved identity and
namespace context explain a changed UID; a root-looking prompt does not.
See [Linux setuid semantics](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/setuid.2.html).

This procedure creates an ordinary text-printing helper, never a SUID helper,
account record or shell persistence file. Hash/metadata checks detect changed
custody, not races in a shared parent. Keep the private-parent prerequisite.
The launched shell can read startup files and retain history; returning and
removing the exact helper do not imply those effects were erased.

## LPRIV-14. An append right, an account and a shell are different results

The DC-4 stdin append and DC-9 two-file append share prepared account bytes,
verification and recovery, not invocation syntax. Omitting tee-like `-a` can
overwrite the original instead of appending. The stdin branch's NOPASSWD and
noninteractive sudo requirement prevents record input from becoming a password
prompt stream. Pipeline exit alone is not proof of correct account bytes;
verify exact state after either success or failure and recover unknown state
out of band. `check-original` is read-only and validates preparation before the
selected manual call; it cannot prevent a later competing writer.

The [GNU tee manual](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/coreutils/tee.1.en.html)
documents standard append/output semantics. It does not establish that a renamed
or custom installed utility is GNU tee. Keep the installed-behavior prerequisite.

DC-9's neighboring source explains a two-file append; the later account record
and successful `su` establish the exercised transition. Neither explains the
missing restoration. This procedure keeps the source-matched append, then adds
independent original custody, exact expected-byte verification and root-side
restoration. It does not claim a neighboring source file authenticates a frozen
binary or that DC-4's stdin append tool has identical arguments.

The account file has seven fields. UID zero is privilege, and an inline password
hash does not imply changing the original root password. Actual PAM/NSS and
password-format support decide whether this temporary account can authenticate;
that is why denied login requires the **pre-existing** recovery route. See
[Linux account-file fields](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/passwd.5.html)
and [OpenSSL password hashing](https://docs.openssl.org/3.3/man1/openssl-passwd/).

The helper does not call sudo, su, append a record, create a home, lock out other
accounts or delete recovery files. Restore requires an already verified native
UID-zero context and only accepts the exact prepared append. It preserves the
existing inode, mode, ownership and xattrs by restoring bytes in place; file
timestamps and login history are not restored. It is not an account-database
transaction lock or a substitute for a quiet disposable lab and tested fallback.
Do not use it while another account manager can change the file. Root within a
namespace or an already-open process needs separate native boundary checks.
`-I` also prevents a neighboring `json.py` or Python environment override from
becoming code in the recovery process. The CLI refuses non-isolated launch
before its non-builtin imports, but cannot retroactively protect Python startup;
use the isolated invocation, not a failed ordinary launch as a safety check.

## LPRIV-15. Shell wildcard expansion creates tar options before tar starts

The scheduled shell expands `*` before GNU tar parses its arguments. Filenames
beginning with `--` can therefore become options only when the job runs from the
same writable directory and passes the unquoted wildcard. A recursive path,
quoted literal, explicit `--` separator, non-GNU tar or different working
directory breaks this procedure's prerequisites.

The proof script records the job's effective identity without opening a shell.
Its result still needs trigger-time and host attribution. Remove the option-like
filenames after the check because leaving them in the consumed directory can
repeat the action at every scheduled run.
